claims.text: Nvidia announced non-binding memoranda of understanding with six asset managers -- Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR -- on 10 August 2026, to establish 'AI Compute Infrastructure Financing Platforms' aiming to mobilize over $500 billion in third-party capital for data-center and GPU-cluster financing
claims.reasoning: Nvidia's own newsroom release states this directly; independently corroborated by Blackstone's own press release (a deal counterparty, not a relay) naming the identical six partners and figure. Also consistently covered by CNBC, Bloomberg, Fortune, DataCenterDynamics.

claims.text: The agreements are memoranda of understanding subject to definitive agreements, not committed or signed capital
claims.reasoning: Nvidia's own release frames the partnerships as subject to execution of definitive agreements; independently echoed by Motley Fool and TradingKey describing these as preliminary, non-binding deals.

claims.text: CEO Jensen Huang said, in a CNBC interview, that Nvidia's own financial backstop would be capped at roughly 25% of any individual project's financing, with the six firms making their own independent lending decisions
claims.reasoning: CNBC's own follow-up piece and Motley Fool both attribute this ~25%/$125B figure and the independent-underwriting framing to Huang's CNBC remarks (Becky Quick, Closing Bell: Overtime, 10 Aug 2026), consistently across two independent outlets.
